不懂温柔，却会默默记住别人的喜好；
不懂离别，却会在失去后第一次流下眼泪。

哪怕世界荒芜，人心冷漠，只要有人愿意对你好，你就值得被爱；只要你愿意去爱，你就拥有了活着的意义。

Harmonia是笨拙的温柔，沉默的深情。

[h1]To be fair, it's a decent story but it isn't without faults.[/h1]

Reading along as the story progressed, I ended up not liking it at some point. For such a simple story, it's told well, as by the end I found I liked it again.

Details will have to be kept to a minimum as I don't want to spoil it, but I almost had it all figured out - thankfully I was still slightly surprised as I didn't predict everything. It's no small feat these days, with so many stories in so many different forms of media, in a world rife with remakes and remasters, to write something unpredictable. The only fault? Probably a bit short, as VNs go.

Something that you can see from the store page screenshots is the enormous text windows covering the art. Sadly it is rife, almost all text windows are that big. While being a VN enjoyer, and art being a major draw into the genre, I actually didn't mind it here as there just wasn't enough art to truly care about whether it was hidden behind text or not.


Ultimately these minor bad points are swept aside in the face of the simple, well-written story. You might get a pop-up at the start about a font you don't have though - just select one you do have and you're good to go. Considering the game length, probably ensure it's discounted before you buy. No guide required for achievements.

Harmonia, developed by VisualArts/Key and published by VisualArts, is a delicate and heartfelt visual novel that embodies the studio’s trademark blend of melancholy, humanism, and emotional catharsis. Set in a distant future where civilization has long since collapsed, it tells the story of Rei, a mechanical boy known as a “Phiroid,” who awakens in a desolate facility with no memory of his past and no ability to feel emotion. As he wanders through a ruined world, he encounters a young woman named Shiona who welcomes him into a small surviving community. What begins as a quiet tale of companionship gradually unfolds into a profound meditation on love, humanity, and the fragile threads that tie hearts together, even in a world left in ruins.

From the very first moments, Harmonia establishes a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere. The world it presents is one of decay and silence, where remnants of human civilization linger like ghosts among the rubble. Yet amid the ashes, there is still warmth—faint but enduring—found in the interactions between Rei and those he meets. The contrast between the bleakness of the setting and the sincerity of the characters gives the story an emotional gravity that slowly builds as the narrative progresses. Shiona, with her gentle optimism and musical spirit, acts as the heart of the story, guiding Rei through the process of rediscovering what it means to feel. Her kindness and unrelenting hope form the emotional axis around which the game revolves, while Rei’s gradual transformation from an emotionless observer into a being capable of empathy and love forms the arc that defines the experience.

The storytelling in Harmonia is linear, unfolding more like a kinetic novel than a traditional branching visual novel. There are no choices to be made, no alternate routes or endings—only a single, deliberate journey that the player is meant to experience in full. This design choice fits perfectly with the tone of the story. Rather than focusing on interactivity or replayability, Harmonia invites players to lose themselves in its atmosphere, to listen, to watch, and to feel. The pacing is measured and patient, with quiet, reflective stretches punctuated by emotional revelations. It is the kind of story that asks the reader to slow down and absorb its subtleties rather than rush toward a conclusion. This simplicity works to the game’s advantage, allowing its themes and characters to breathe without distraction.

The art direction is classic Key: soft pastel tones, expressive character designs, and warm light that filters through even the most desolate landscapes. Despite its post-apocalyptic setting, Harmonia never feels grim; instead, it carries a sense of serene melancholy, like sunlight shining through dust. Every scene, from the barren wastelands to the cozy interiors of Shiona’s home, is painted with care and an attention to mood that enhances the emotional experience. The use of color plays an important role in expressing Rei’s awakening emotions—early sequences feel washed out and muted, while later moments take on a richer, warmer palette as he begins to understand joy, pain, and love. The soundtrack, composed by Shinji Orito and other Key veterans, is a standout element that reinforces the game’s tone. The delicate piano melodies and gentle orchestral arrangements evoke both sorrow and serenity, underscoring each emotional beat with precision. The theme songs, particularly Shiona’s music, act not only as motifs within the story but as emotional bridges between characters and player.

At its core, Harmonia is a story about rediscovering humanity in a world that has forgotten it. Through Rei’s journey, the game explores questions that have long fascinated Key’s storytellers: what defines a person, what gives life meaning, and how love endures even in the face of loss. The fact that Rei begins the story as a machine incapable of emotion gives his evolution a poignant weight. His interactions with Shiona and the young girl Tipi—each representing different facets of human experience—become lessons in empathy, pain, and forgiveness. The writing balances introspection and tenderness, steering clear of sentimentality even as it builds toward an emotional climax. When the final revelations come, they feel both inevitable and devastating, offering closure without betraying the quiet tone that defines the story.

While the narrative succeeds in delivering a moving and memorable experience, it also bears some of the limitations of Key’s shorter works. The brevity of the story—typically completed in around four or five hours—means that its worldbuilding is more suggestive than comprehensive. The post-apocalyptic setting provides a striking backdrop but remains largely unexplored beyond what serves the emotional narrative. Some players may find the pacing uneven, as the slow, meditative opening eventually gives way to a rush of revelations near the end. Those accustomed to Key’s sprawling narratives, like Clannad or Little Busters!, may feel that Harmonia resolves its themes too swiftly. Yet for many, its conciseness will be part of its charm; it never overstays its welcome, and its emotional beats are all the more impactful for their focus.

Visually, the Full HD edition of Harmonia released later brought meaningful improvements that modernized the experience without altering its spirit. The sharper character art, higher-resolution backgrounds, and fully voiced performances enhance immersion, breathing new life into the story. The voice acting, particularly for Shiona and Tipi, adds depth to the emotional resonance of the dialogue, making the characters feel even more real. Combined with the original’s already evocative art and music, these updates reaffirm the game’s timeless appeal and make it accessible to new audiences while preserving what made it special to begin with.

Despite its simplicity, Harmonia manages to leave a lasting impression because of its sincerity. It never tries to overwhelm the player with complexity or shock—it simply tells a story that feels genuine, heartfelt, and deeply human. The emotions it evokes linger well beyond the closing credits, and its central message—about love as the essence of life and the bridge between souls—resonates with quiet power. Harmonia may not reach the same scale or fame as Key’s larger works, but it stands proudly among them as a distilled expression of what the studio does best: touching hearts through fragile beauty. It’s a reminder that even in a broken world, music, kindness, and the simple act of feeling can bring light to the darkest places.

In the end, Harmonia is not just a post-apocalyptic love story—it is a reflection on what it means to be alive. It’s about the bonds that connect people, the pain that defines them, and the hope that endures even after everything else fades. With its graceful writing, haunting visuals, and emotional authenticity, it captures the essence of Key’s storytelling tradition in a concentrated form. It is quiet, contemplative, and devastatingly beautiful, a game that speaks softly but leaves echoes long after it ends. For anyone who values emotional depth and poetic simplicity in storytelling, Harmonia is an experience that will stay with them, like a half-remembered melody that continues to play long after the music stops.

Rating: 9/10

Pelo que tenho observado, meu tempo de leitura foi bem mais longo do que a média. Culpa minha, pois sou lento para ler. Mas, conforme a história avançava, consegui acelerar o ritmo gradativamente.

Harmonia tem uma história no geral agradável. Ela segue um esquema de capítulos, o que eu gostei, pois deixa o enredo organizado, e torna fácil de reler partes específicas se você tiver vontade. Os primeiros 3 ou 4 capítulos parecem um pouco sem rumo na 1ª leitura, mas tudo é uma construção que faz sentido mais tarde. Por mais que esse trecho possa aparentar ter uma "gordurinha", isso faz diferença para desenvolver a relação dos dois personagens principais. Não vou negar, o começo deu um pouco de preguiça, pois é muito "água com açúcar". Shiona e Rei são bem inocentes, e o menino ainda é consideravelmente apático, então a interação deles é básica e até tediosa inicialmente. Além disso, as partes focadas na personagem Tipi podem ser um pouco cansativas devido ao tom excessivamente melancólico, embora isso tenha sentido temático. No entanto, os capítulos se tornaram mais interessantes à medida que eu progredi. Os últimos dois, que compreendem o final, são bastante satisfatórios. Por mais que eu já tivesse sacado parte do plot twist antes, a explicação completa é bem legal, inclusive mais rica em detalhes do que eu esperava, e certamente foi o ponto mais alto da novel.

O visual é muito simples e econômico. Existem poucos CGs para ilustrar melhor as cenas, senti falta deles em vários momentos. Também achei os backgrounds bem repetitivos, seria bom ter mais variedade. Mas acredito que este tenha sido um projeto pequeno feito em paralelo com outros maiores, então é compreensível que seja assim. Pelo lado positivo, gostei dos efeitos sutis, como a animação nas rachuras dos sprites e o granulado sobre os cenários externos, imitando uma tempestade de areia.

Mas, independentemente do fato de este ser um título comemorativo da desenvolvedora, e não um projeto minimamente ambicioso, a qualidade da trilha sonora é muito alta. Sou um grande fã dos músicos que trabalham para a Key, pois nesse quesito é muito difícil sair decepcionado de suas obras. Além de serem atmosféricas e combinarem perfeitamente com o tom da história, as faixas são marcantes e eu certamente vou ouvi-las mais vezes. Destaco as seguintes: "#6 Tristitia", "#7 Pecado" e "#14 Spero" (seguindo a numeração da seção "music", dentro do jogo). As canções-tema também são excelentes.

No fim, considero o saldo positivo dentro do que a novel se propõe, e saio satisfeito desta experiência. Como minha primeira VN concluída, Harmonia serviu também como um exercício de velocidade de leitura pra mim, além de ter enriquecido um pouco meu vocabulário na língua inglesa. Aliás, nesse tópico, só não gostei muito do modo como as falas da Tipi são traduzidas, não acho que termos como "yeah" combinem com a personalidade dela (mas isso já é nitpicking da minha parte).

正如其名字一样，本作将“和谐”作为大主题，立意很深远很棒，不少话语都引人深思。本作很巧妙地把大道理隐藏在了抒情之下，使得文字的说教气息并不浓厚，这是比较优秀的一点

需要改进的地方——当然是有的。
情节方面，把所有谜题的揭示都放在了后期的一个节点上。这样的做法既使前期的节奏过慢、缺乏层层深入的快感，也使这一节点的解释过于冗长。繁多的解释使得情节中很多具有对比意义、想要引人思考的发展就这样赤裸裸地暴露在了不加修饰的情节中，导致主旨的表达过于刻意，不够自然、深刻
其次是角色的塑造上。诗音那这个人物过于正面了，相比起一个人物她更像是一种象征，一种“纯粹的爱与善意”的符号。这样的写法使得诗音那死的时候象征意味更加浓厚，也更强调了作品的主旨。但我刚才也说了，本作的主旨表达过于刻意不够深刻，因此在这一点上我认为，将诗音那塑造得更像一个活生生的人物，以此来加强死亡时的抒情爆发，是一种更好的方案。

[code]那是，献给提比的旋律。
我的脸颊滑过热热的东西。
流过我的下颚，滴落在提比的脸颊上。
提比明明没有在哭泣，看起来却像是在哭。
我抱起提比。
这小小的身躯，再也不会动了。
这口中，再也不会发出声音。
这双手，再也无法描绘图画。
这就是“死亡”。
我的头上传来温暖。
诗音那抱紧了我。
突然眼眶发热。
这就是溢出的感情。是无法忍受的痛苦，是不可压抑的撕心裂肺……是无尽的悲伤。
有生以来我第一次流“泪”了。[/code]

说到这相信明眼人也看出来了，相比于诗音那我更喜欢本作的“提比”这个角色。一方面提比作为“蓝蓝”的少女，登场时就满脸哭泣，一副非常需要人保护的样子，但与其相反的则是说到图书时异常靠谱的表现。角色的弱气与靠谱同时在提比身上体现出来，使人立马就对她感兴趣起来，而通过后续剧情的补充，我认为提比也成为了本作塑造最为立体的角色——若是只有诗音那的“爱”传承下来的话，我一定是不太能感受到作品所包含的另一个意思的，但与此同时提比的“知识”也一同赠予了男主，这使得“传递”这个小主题也变得明朗起来

[code]想找到那样的世界肯定困难至极吧。

一场关于人性，情感与人类的探讨。
本来一开始还在琢磨为什么岛国人有那么多人和机器人相恋的故事。一开始还以为是因为机器人不会怀孕来着。。。现在思索一下，也许是拥有情感的机器人更纯粹，也更有可能是人类想象中最美好的模样。那种机器人的所思所想几乎全来自于人类的指令设定，换而言之，只要人类想要机器人是啥样的，那ta就是啥样的，完全取决于人类输入的指令，那大概完美女友完美男友什么的应该也能实现罢。ta可以毫无理由的天性善良，也可以毫无理由的天性邪恶。
一开始的剧情较为普通甚至平平无奇，一直到了反转的那一刻才到达了作品的高潮。只不过我个人对于电车难题这种东西还是有点讨厌的。
以下吐槽涉及剧透：
真是个讽刺的世界观啊。。。有情感的人类几乎见不着，无情感的人类却奴役着同族，并认为感情是愚蠢之物，在这末世之中，最像人类的反而是那帮保存着人类文明，并准备随时把文明交还给人类，拥有着情感的智能机器人们。男主刚苏醒的时候也是个不知情感为何物的人类，不会去爱，但在机器人的引导下，觉醒了被封存的情感，并在未来重新开辟了拥有蓝天白云的乌托邦。
不过我还是有点事情想吐槽，那就是那些反派虽然嘴上说着生产力不能落下，但奴役制明明也不算什么高生产力的制度，按他们的科技水平，生产关系本不应如此。。。所以我估计，他们相比于生产力，更在意如何报复有情感的种族，要论生产力的话还有更文明的方法。。。还有就是，一开始男主误认自己是机器，那时候我就在想，男主也忒像人类了，拥有那么丰富的情感表现，后来看了反转之后果真是这么回事。。。
但是，不推荐购买，因为这部作品的质量实在赶不上key社的其它作品的平均水准。虽说一分钱一分货，galgame定价高乃是霓虹传统，但这个剧情感觉还是配不上这个价。。。我为什么不拿这钱去好好吃顿饭呢

Nonetheless, Harmonia explored a rather interesting concept of human emotions and the legacy succession of civilization; it was a fun experience.
